title: Relative Gaussian Tail Accuracy for the Gram-Schmidt Walk Design

tldr: For the existing randomized retained-pivot Gram--Schmidt walk and population Horvitz--Thompson causal estimator, the maximal actual-variance relative Gaussian-tail window is proved on the full maintained bounded, well-conditioned fixed-dimensional class: \(D_n(r_n)\to0\) if and only if \(r_n=o(n^{1/4})\). The quantitative actual-law upper bound is paired with a saturated legal zero-row witness, whose critical ratio at \(x=tn^{1/4}\) is \(\exp(-t^4/(3c))\). The maintained class is a proper subclass of the published CDG sequence domain; the stronger converse transfers to that wider domain, while positive calibration is proved on the maintained class. Simultaneous oracle Gaussian calibration down to two-sided nominal levels \(\alpha_n\) holds exactly when \(\log(1/\alpha_n)=o(\sqrt n)\).
gap: The published randomized-pivot CLT describes central fluctuations, while available finite-sample concentration calibrates a ridge or projection proxy. Their conclusions do not identify actual-variance relative Gaussian tails.
fill: Evaluate \(D_n\) with a primitive all-class upper theorem and matched actual-law obstructions. Convert its admissible ranges into oracle relative noncoverage guarantees for the unchanged population HT map.
